Marion County by the numbers

Where is the Marion County Recorder's Office and when can you reach it?

The Marion County Recorder's Office is in the City-County Building at 200 E. Washington Street, Suite T-741, Indianapolis, IN 46204. The counter is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, and the main number is 317.327.4020.

Phone calls are answered from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily, and messages are returned within one to two business days. The office says email to recorder@indy.gov gets the fastest response.

The office keeps permanent public records of property transactions, including deeds, liens, mortgages, easements and survey maps. Its page describes more than 11 million records in its care.

One change affects anyone who used to pick up a blank form there. Effective September 29, 2026, the office no longer provides forms or documents for recording. The stated reason is protecting owners from property fraud.

How do you record a deed in Marion County?

You record a deed in Marion County by first getting it stamped at the Assessor's Office, then submitting it to the Recorder with the fee. The county lists the steps on its Record Your Deed page.

  1. Gather the exact name of the current owner and the legal description. The Assessor's property report card or the current tax bill can supply them.
  2. Prepare the deed. The grantor is the person now on title and the grantee is the person who will be listed as the new owner. The county recommends an attorney.
  3. Sign and notarize the document.
  4. Take or mail it to the Assessor for the transfer stamp, with a separate check or money order for each office.
  5. The Recorder records it and returns it to you.
  6. Apply for any deductions you qualify for through the Marion County Auditor.

Documents can be submitted by mail, through e-recording partners or in person. Marion County has leaned heavily on electronic filing. In November 2025 the office recorded 8,764 documents, and 7,948 of them came in as e-recordings.

What does it cost to record a deed in Marion County?

The county's deed page lists $35.00 per document at the Recorder, plus $10.00 per parcel per document and $20.00 for each sales disclosure at the Assessor. Those are separate offices, so they are paid separately.

ChargeAmountWhere
Recording fee for a deed$35.00 per documentRecorder
Transfer fee$10.00 per parcel per documentAssessor
Sales disclosure form$20.00 per form, if requiredAssessor
Copies of recorded documents$1 per page up to 11 by 17 inches (state schedule)Recorder

The state schedule in Indiana Code 36-2-7-10 sets a base fee of $25 for a deed and $55 for a mortgage. For a county with a consolidated city, the statute and the State Board of Accounts recorder manual describe extra pieces: an optional housing trust fee of $2.50 for the first page and $1 for each added page, an identification security fee of $2, and an optional affordable housing fee of up to $10. The county's published $35 figure is the number to plan around, and the Recorder's fee schedule governs if your document has extra pages or unusual features.

Oversized pages cost more under the state schedule, $25 for the first and $5 for each additional. Military discharge papers are recorded free of charge, per the county.

What must a Marion County deed include to be accepted?

A deed has to be notarized, carry specific statements and meet formatting rules, or the office will reject it. The county's requirements page cites Indiana Code for each point.

  • Notarization under IC 32-21-2-3.
  • A statement under penalties of perjury that reasonable care was taken to redact Social Security numbers, plus the name of the person who prepared the instrument (IC 36-2-11-15).
  • Names of signers and witnesses printed identically throughout and typed under each signature (IC 36-2-11-16).
  • Two-inch top and bottom margins on the first and last pages for the recording stamp. Without them, an extra page is added (IC 36-2-11-16.5).
  • A street address where tax statements should be mailed (IC 32-21-2-3).
  • For a power of attorney signing, the document number of the power of attorney with the signature.

The notary's name must match the commission, with the county of residence, the commission expiration date and the date of notarization. Seals for commissions issued or renewed after July 1, 2018 must also show the words "notary public," "State of Indiana," "seal," and the seven-digit commission number.

Re-recording a document means paying the original fee again and stating the reason at the top of the page. The office asks for a self-addressed stamped envelope with paper returns.

Is there a transfer tax or sales disclosure in Marion County?

The county page for the Assessor describes transfer and sales disclosure fees, not a percentage transfer tax. Marion County lists a $10 transfer fee per parcel and $20 per sales disclosure form. We did not find a percentage transfer tax on the official pages we read.

Under Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5-3, the parties must complete and sign a sales disclosure form before a conveyance document is filed with the county auditor. The county assessor reviews it for accuracy and completeness and, if it passes, approves it and returns it to a party for filing. Marion County asks filers to prepare the form in the Properly system at forms.properlytaxes.com, then print and sign it.

The Assessor's counter at Room W121 will not process documents after 4 p.m., and it accepts cash, checks for the exact amount and credit cards, with a small extra charge on cards. The Assessor cannot help prepare a deed, so use an attorney or title company.

How does the Recorder help protect owners from deed fraud?

Marion County offers a free Property Fraud Alert service for Marion County residents, promoted by the Recorder. Sign-up is at propertyfraudalert.com/INMARION.

The office reported 636 sign-ups in November 2025 and has put the alert on billboards. The same fraud concern is behind the 2026 change that ends the office's own blank forms.

For a seller this has a practical side. If you inherit a house or own one that sits empty, signing up is a free step worth taking.

Other services listed by the Recorder include a survivorship affidavit to remove a deceased owner from title, copies of deeds, a recording fee refund claim, and online search of real estate records.

What should a Marion County seller know about recording and closing?

Most sellers never record anything themselves, because the title or escrow company handles the stamp and the recording. The point of knowing the steps is to spot delays.

Delays usually come from one of these:

  • A missing notary detail or a name that differs from the vested deed.
  • A legal description that does not match the records.
  • A deed submitted without the Assessor stamp.
  • An unreleased mortgage or lien that still appears in the Recorder's index.

Marion County is the most populous of the Indiana counties covered in this guide, and its Recorder holds a large archive. Title work on an older house can reach back through many owners, which is why a clean chain of title is worth checking early. If you are weighing a quick sale of a house with title questions, a written offer from a cash buyer lets you see the terms before you commit.

More questions about Marion County, IN County Recorder

How much does it cost to record a deed in Marion County, Indiana?

The county's Record Your Deed page lists $35.00 per document at the Recorder. The Assessor charges separately: $10.00 per parcel per document, and $20.00 for each sales disclosure when one is required.

Do I record a deed before or after the Assessor stamps it?

After. In Marion County the Assessor's transfer stamp is required before the Recorder can record the deed. Take the stamped deed to the Recorder in Room T-741.

Can I e-record a deed in Marion County?

Yes. The Recorder's Office accepts documents by mail, through its e-recording partners or in person. In November 2025, 7,948 of 8,764 recorded documents were e-recordings.

Does the Marion County Recorder still hand out deed forms?

No. The office says that from September 29, 2026 it no longer provides forms or documents for recording. Have an attorney or title company draft the deed.

What phone number and email reach the Marion County Recorder?

Call 317.327.4020 or email recorder@indy.gov. Calls are answered from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily, and email is the fastest route according to the office.

Is there a percentage transfer tax in Marion County?

The official pages we read list flat fees only: $10 per parcel for the transfer and $20 per sales disclosure at the Assessor, plus the Recorder's fee. Ask your title company to confirm the total for your sale.
